newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end 2.72 pct down on baht, Somprasong.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end 2.72 pct down on baht, Somprasong.

text.p: Market worries about the baht recent depreciation and an interest payment default by a property firm triggered more heavy selloff of Thai stocks on Wednesday, brokers said.
"The index slipped on poor market sentiment related to baht's recent depreciation and Somprasong Land's failure to meet an interest payment deadline," said Payuha Boonsiri of Nithipat Capital.
The SET index ended 20.83 points, or 2.72 percent, lower at a near 54-month low of 744.59 on 4.6 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index dropped 1.80 points to 54.50.
Somprasong Land said in a filing to the Stock Exchange of Thailand before the market closed that its payment default could be attributed to a prolonged slump of the Thai property market.
It said independent appraisers would be commissioned by the company's management to assess its assets and liabilities.
A financial advisor of Somprasong said earlier the company had failed to make a $3.1 million interest payment on its $80 million Euroconvertible debentures due on February 4.
"Investors are pondering about credibility of Thai firms which have issued ECDs abroad following the Somprasong case," said a broker at a foreign brokerage house.
